title: Preservation on the proved finite-Tor domains
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ range over separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use bounded constructibility [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], its cohomological intervals [def-weil-constructible-intervals], finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and the coefficient twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].
At this finite coefficient stage the following hold:

1. **(i)** $Lf^*$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
1. **(ii)** Derived tensor carries
$D^b_{ctf}\times D^b_{ctf}$ into $D^b_{ctf}$; if the two inputs have
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, the output has Tor amplitude in
$[a+c,b+d]$.
For $K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, internal Hom also belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
If $K,L$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ and
$m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and $\dim X\leq m$, then $R\mathcal Hom(K,L)$ has Tor amplitude in
$[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$; if moreover $K$ is site-perfect, it has Tor
amplitude in the sharper interval $[c-b,d-a]$.
The elementary formula $R\mathcal Hom(K,L)=K^\vee\otimes^L L$
with coefficient dual $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom(K,A_X)$, and the
dimension-free interval $[c-b,d-a]$, still require
a site-perfect first argument (for the origin
$i:\{0\}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1$, both $i_*A$ and $A$ have Tor
amplitude $[0,0]$, while $R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)=i_*A(-1)[-2]$ has
cohomology in degree $2$);
the general preservation assertion uses geometric Verdier duality.
1. **(iii)** $Rf_*$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$; for input Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ and
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and $\dim X\leq d$, the output has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$.
1. **(iv)** $Rf_!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$.
1. **(v)** The exceptional adjoint on the constructible
coefficient category satisfies $Rf^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$ and carries
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
For nonnegative integer dimension bounds $d_X,d_Y$ with
$\dim X\leq d_X$ and $\dim Y\leq d_Y$
[def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and input Tor interval $[a,b]$,
one output interval is $[a-2d_X,b+2d_Y]$.
For nonempty schemes the bounds may be their dimensions;
for an empty scheme the bound may be zero.
1. **(vi)** For every separated finite-type $X/k$,
$D_X=R\mathcal Hom_X(-,Ra_X^!A)$ is a contravariant exact
anti-equivalence with $K\simeq D_XD_XK$, by the geometric
Verdier-biduality theorem on this domain.
1. **(vii)** On the finite-Tor constructible domains,
finite coefficient quotients commute with pullback, tensor, both
direct images, general internal Hom, Verdier duality and the
exceptional adjoint, preserving their evaluation and adjunction maps.
For derived-complete
integral objects, $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)=D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$.
General internal Hom and the exceptional adjoint preserve this
category; Verdier duality is an anti-equivalence on it, with the
canonical finite reductions of these operations. These conclusions
pass to the bounded constructible categories at $E$ and
$\Qlb$, with their specified coefficient-passage operations.
The elementary site-perfect formula in (ii) retains its stated
hypothesis. No unrestricted unbounded pro-etale exceptional
adjunction is asserted here.

proof.text: For (i), apply sf_pullback_finiteTorConstructible from lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude. The private constantPullbackModel of lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-equivalence identifies the two ordinary pullbacks by uniqueness of left adjoints. Mapping this natural isomorphism through derived localization identifies the ringed pullback with finiteDerivedPullback. Transport finite-Tor constructibility across that isomorphism; bounded constructibility is closed under isomorphisms by lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated, and Tor amplitude transports by composing representative isomorphisms.

For tensor in (ii), choose complex preimages of both derived objects and a K-flat resolution of the first by lem-pc-kflat-resolution. Apply finiteCoefficient_tensor_ctf of lem-sf-tensor-ctf to these representatives. The normalized one-K-flat comparison from lem-sfb-ringed-tensor-comparison-extension, followed by functoriality on the resolution and representative isomorphisms, identifies the computed tensor with finiteIntrinsicDerivedTensor. Transport constructibility and each ordered Tor interval across the resulting isomorphism. This gives both preservation and [a+c,b+d].

The site-perfect refinement of (ii), including its coefficient-dual tensor formula with the specified unit and its [c-b,d-a] interval, is precisely lem-sf-intrinsic-site-perfect-hom-window. This split retains the local perfect-model argument of the blueprint and assumes no geometric dimension correction.

For arbitrary $K,L$ in the finite-Tor constructible category, [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom] gives bounded constructibility, finite Tor amplitude, and the interval $[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$ on either site. Its hypotheses are satisfied because $X$ is separated and finite type and $m$ is a nonnegative dimension bound. This proves the general internal-Hom assertion; the preceding steps give its site-perfect refinement.

For the origin $i:\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_k$, work first on the etale site. [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] gives stalk $A$ at the origin and zero elsewhere for $i_*A$. Exact and conservative geometric stalks, [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], together with [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar], show that tensoring with $i_*A$ preserves injections. Thus $i_*A$ and $A$ have Tor interval $[0,0]$. The canonical comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] identifies $\nu^*Ri_*A$ with $Ri_*\nu^*A$; etale exactness of $i_*$ follows from the same stalk formula. [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](i) therefore gives the same two Tor intervals for the pro-etale sheaves, where $i_*$ is exact by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] since its complement is quasi-compact.

source.place: paragraph 1, flatness of the origin example

proof.text: On the pro-etale site of the Noetherian $\mathbf A^1_k$, specialize [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] to $s=i$ and $P=M=A$: $R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)\cong Ri_*Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}A$, with $Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}$ the right adjoint of $i_*$ on the ambient unbounded categories. This is not by definition the constructible functor $Ri^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; compare them. With $j:\mathbf G_{m,k}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_k$, [lem-exc-proetale-support-triangle] gives a triangle $i_*Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}A\to A\to Rj_*j^*A\to$. By [prop-sf-localization-all-stages](1'),(3') at $\Lambda=A$, the last two vertices lie in $D^b_{ctf}$, triangulated by [lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated], hence so does the first. The counit $i^*i_*\to\mathrm{id}$ is invertible by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful] and $i^*$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ by (3'), so $Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}A\in D^b_c(\operatorname{Spec}k,A)$. For $Q$ there, the ambient adjunction and clause (2) give natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_*Q,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Q,Ri^!A)$; Yoneda gives $Ri^!_{\mathrm{amb}}A\cong Ri^!A$. [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity] with $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $c=1$ states $Ri^!A\cong A(-1)[-2]$ for every $n\geq1$. Exactness [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] gives $R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)\cong i_*A(-1)[-2]$. Its degree-two cohomology is nonzero: the rank-one twist is nonzero and $i_*$ is fully faithful by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful]. This holds for ramified $E$ and every $n$.

source.place: paragraph 1, purity and supported Hom in the origin example

proof.text: For (iii), apply finiteCoefficientDirectImage_boundedConstructible_torAmplitude of cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale for each input Tor interval and each dimension bound. Existence of a finite source dimension bound gives finite Tor amplitude of the output. For (iv), apply the compact-support preservation clause of operations_preserve from lem-coef-finite-exceptional to the given compactification. Its operations use exactly sfIntrinsicCompactSupport.

For clauses (v)-(vi), use the existing finite exceptional adjunction and its natural dual formula from lem-coef-finite-exceptional. Compare the chosen intrinsic closed unit with the coefficient sheaf in degree zero: choose the closed monoidal structure of lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal, compare the two tensor-right functors as left adjoints to the same internal Hom, and apply the right and left unitors. Mapping this unit isomorphism by the specified exceptional functor identifies sfStabilityFiniteVerdier with FiniteExceptional.dual, naturally in its argument. HasCompactification is a proposition, so the two structural compactification selections agree. operations_preserve gives exceptional preservation. Apply lem-sf-finite-intrinsic-verdier-bounds on Y, lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude and the existing pullback comparison, then lem-sf-finite-intrinsic-verdier-bounds on X. The resulting interval is [-(-a)-2dX,-(-b-2dY)]=[a-2dX,b+2dY]; transport it through the natural dual formula. thm-fix-general-biduality separately supplies both fixed-scalar canonical biduality conclusions. Restriction of the adjunction is definitionally FiniteExceptional.adjunction. Whisker the natural dual formula by the two Verdier comparisons, using opposite isomorphisms in the contravariant positions; cancel the fully faithful inclusion to obtain the stated natural constructible formula.

proof.text: For the intrinsic exact anti-equivalence, lem-sf-finite-intrinsic-verdier-bounds first restricts the intrinsic dual functor to the finite-Tor constructible subcategory. The finite tensor presentations and signed natural symmetries of lem-sf-integral-verdier-signed-calculus have the evaluation normalization required by lem-sf-finite-intrinsic-verdier-biduality. Apply that finite biduality theorem to each object and its supplied Tor interval. The existing signed_delta_natural helper of thm-coef-integral-verdier makes these components a natural isomorphism from identity to double dual. Its proved dual_equivalence helper gives an equivalence. The unit-induced Verdier comparison identifies its inclusion with the specified sfStabilityFiniteVerdier. For exactness, use lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-universes at the actual finite coefficient universe, transfer its shift structure through this natural comparison, and apply map_distinguished. This argument makes no completeness assumption on the finite input and uses the finite geometric biduality result, not a site-perfect computation.

For finiteTor_stability_quotients, identify normalized strict-tower scalar restriction with direct quotient restriction by compactSupportModuleRes_eq from [lem-weil-compact-support-coefficient-transition]. First prove equality of the positive-level finite quotient sheaf maps, then apply congrArg pbcDerivedExtend; this identifies FiniteExceptional.reduction with direct quotient extension without unfolding the chosen derived functor. The quotient calculus adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] and uniqueness of left adjoints identify coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived with FiniteExceptional.reduction; [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] then gives finite-Tor preservation. The intrinsic clauses of [thm-coef-finite-hom] give invertibility of the specified internal-Hom reduction and the full CoefficientEvaluationCompatible datum. Obtain a finite dimension bound and use [lem-coef-integral-dualizing-finite-bounds] to put the actual finite dualizing term in the finite-Tor domain. Apply the same Hom coefficient comparison to that term. The intrinsic dualizing reduction of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing], composed with the adjoint-uniqueness isomorphism, is invertible. Applying internal Hom to this isomorphism proves invertibility of the displayed Verdier reduction. For compact support, [lem-finite-compact-support-scalar-comparison] proves invertibility of the ordinary scalar-adjunction transpose of compact support of the scalar unit followed by sfCompactSupportRestriction. Its reduced-input constructibility hypothesis follows from FiniteExceptional.reduction_preserves. The normalized and ordinary scalar adjunctions are presented in the same intrinsic derived categories, through definitions containing precisely the existing adjunction data. The proved generic unit calculation sfStabilityScalarMate_eq_inverse identifies the pointwise scalar transpose with the original inverse mate. Naturality of the restriction square and unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app prove sfStabilityScalarMate_eq_transported: changing the scalar left adjoints conjugates the mate by their canonical uniqueness isomorphisms. The support comparison is now expressed as this conjugate. At each object, unfold the two packaging definitions and compose the two isomorphisms with the ordinary scalar mate, whose invertibility is exactly the cited compact-support scalar theorem. This checks the factors directly rather than reconstructing a large concrete inverse-mate expression. Thus the specified sfStabilitySupportReduction component is invertible, including identity quotients. The public sfStabilityQuotientPbcRestrictionEquality writes the existing restriction equality in the ordinary pbcDerivedRestrict API. The support interface explicitly names its intrinsic category instances; sfStabilityFiniteCategory is exactly inferInstance. No functor, adjunction, restriction square or canonical map is replaced mathematically.

The still-open geometric quotient clause retains the following route. For pullback use the scalar-balancing comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. For ordinary direct image, [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] gives the counit-defined comparison and its coefficient cocycle. For a pro-etale constructible input, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) gives a bounded constructible etale representative, and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) transfers its finite Tor interval. Thus the etale-origin assertion applies. For the exceptional functor, transport the coefficient comparison of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] through the specified comparison functors; its mate equation is the displayed counit identity.

The Lean predicates sfIntegralConstructible and boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegral agree: [lem-sf-derived-complete-legacy-comparison] identifies completeness, and their uniform cohomological support conditions are the same inequalities. For a derived-complete integral input $K$, its residue reduction $K_1$ has cohomology in some finite interval. [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] gives that same Tor interval for every canonical reduction $K_n$ and explicitly concludes $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)=D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$. For integral $K,L$, [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom] gives preservation by ambient internal Hom and a uniform reduction interval; [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] identifies its canonical finite reductions and evaluations. [thm-coef-integral-verdier] supplies the exact duality anti-equivalence, its canonical reductions and biduality. These nodes supply the integral assertions directly. For the chosen integral dualizing object, extract its normalized counit reduction isomorphisms from [prop-coef-integral-dualizing], then apply [thm-coef-integral-verdier]. Its restricted dual, anti-equivalence and triangle exactness are definitionally the displayed integral Verdier functor. The displayed integral Verdier reduction is the integral Hom comparison followed by internal Hom of the normalized dualizing reduction. Both factors are isomorphisms; functorial preservation and composition prove invertibility of that very morphism.

proof.text: For finiteTor_stability_integral_images, take the exact coherent support tower from lem-weil-compact-support-representative-independence. Its integral constructible realization is naturally isomorphic after inclusion to that tower followed by its published total right derived inverse limit. The package identifies its chosen tower and chosen total right derived inverse limit with exactly the choices used by sfStabilityIntegralSupportAmbient; the apparent coefficient-universe presentations agree definitionally. Transport constructibility across the resulting object isomorphism using lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated. For exceptional preservation, apply integral Verdier preservation on Y, completed pullback preservation from lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible, and integral Verdier preservation on X. The canonical integral Verdier reductions already proved above identify each reduced dual with finite intrinsic duality. For pullback choose a good K-flat representative, use its invertible integralPullbackFiniteComparison, map the unit-normalized integralFinitePullbackModel through complexes and localization, and use the representative reduction isomorphism. Thus reduction of completed pullback is finite pullback of the reduction. Finite intrinsic duality changes [a,b] to [-b-2dY,-a]; finite pullback preserves this interval; duality on X changes it to [-(-a)-2dX,-(-b-2dY)]=[a-2dX,b+2dY]. Transport each interval along the actual reduction isomorphism. No integral exceptional adjunction is assumed for preservation or these bounds, and no new unproved intermediate statement is introduced.

direct images, general internal Hom and the exceptional adjoint preserve
this category ([sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability], [sk-thm-existence]); Verdier duality is an anti-equivalence
on it ([sk-thm-pd-verdier-duality]). Reduction modulo $\pi_E^n$ and
extension of scalars commute with all of these operations, preserving their
evaluation and adjunction maps ([sk-prop-scalar-six]).

proof.text:
For (i), bounded constructibility is
[lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible], and
flat inverse image in [lem-exc-constant-inverse-image-flat]
preserves the Tor interval of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
For (ii), the Tor intervals add under derived tensor: with bounded
flat models of $K$ in $[a,b]$ and of $L$ in $[c,d]$, the total tensor
complex is a bounded flat model in $[a+c,b+d]$. Refine the
finite constructible stratifications for the two complexes; the
bounded tensor complexes on each stratum have finite locally constant
cohomology, which gives constructibility. If $K$ is site-perfect
in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], a bounded finite-projective
local model $P$ in $[a,b]$ computes its dual and identifies
$R\mathcal Hom(K,L)=K^\vee\otimes^L L$ by
[prop-sf-dualizable-hom]. The tensor argument proves Hom
preservation in that case, and since $P^\vee$ is a bounded
finite-projective complex in $[-b,-a]$, the tensor bound gives the
interval $[c-b,d-a]$; this is the sharper assertion of
[thm-sf-hom-ctf], whose argument is local on the site and so applies
on either site; on the pro-étale site this is [cor-sf-hom-ctf-proetale-unconditional]. For a general constructible finite-Tor
first argument, use [cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom], whose
proof uses geometric Verdier biduality and gives the
dimension-dependent interval $[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$. The displayed
example shows the dimension-free interval fails without
site-perfectness: $R\mathcal Hom(i_*A,A)=i_*Ri^!A$ by adjunction, and
$Ri^!A=A(-1)[-2]$ by purity for the point in the smooth curve.

Clause (iii) is [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale]: its etale
calculation is [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude], with the
uniform all-sheaf cohomological bound supplied by
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing]. That calculation uses a
bounded-above free resolution of a finite constant coefficient and
the cohomological bound; it does not use a projection formula for an
arbitrary sheaf on the target. For (iv), choose a compactification
$f=pj$ and use [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].
Extension by zero $j_!$ is exact and commutes with tensor, as is
seen on stalks, so preserves the Tor interval and constructibility.
Apply (iii) to the proper factor $p$.

Clause (v) is the preservation result for the exceptional inverse
image, assembled from the closed and smooth cases. For a closed immersion
$i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with $\dim T\leq d$, the open complement satisfies
the open-complement condition with $c=2d$ by
[thm-pur-open-complement-unconditional], so [prop-exc-closed-tor]
carries bounded constructible input of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ to bounded
constructible output of Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d+1]$. For $f$ smooth of pure
relative dimension $d$, purity identifies $Rf^!$ with $Lf^*(-)(d)[2d]$ and
[cor-pur-smooth-admissibility] gives the shift $-2d$ on both intervals.
A general $f$ is, on affine charts $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$, a closed
immersion $U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ followed by the smooth
projection, and composing the two cases along the charts is
[thm-pur-general-admissibility]; its open-complement hypothesis on the
charts is discharged by [cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum], so it is a
theorem and not an assumption. At the finite stage $A=A_{E,n}$ and for every
separated finite-type $f$ of the statement this is
[thm-sf-preservation-class](2): $Rf^!$ carries $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into
$D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, with no ambient datum assumed on that category. With this
preservation, the finite dual formula and adjunction of
[lem-coef-finite-exceptional] identify $Rf^!$ with $D_Xf^*D_Y$ on this
domain; applying the finite duality bound on $Y$, ordinary pullback, and
the finite duality bound on $X$ gives the displayed output interval. Clause (vi) is
[thm-fix-general-biduality] at finite coefficients;
its geometric proof supplies the
anti-equivalence and is not replaced by the site-perfect calculation
in (ii).

For (vii), use [lem-fix-operation-reduction] for pullback,
tensor and compact supports, and [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]
for ordinary direct image. General finite internal-Hom and duality
comparisons are [thm-coef-finite-hom], [cor-coef-finite-verdier];
the exceptional comparison is [lem-coef-finite-exceptional].
Their proofs compare the specified evaluations and adjunction maps.

For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, the equality $D^b_c=D^b_{ctf}$ is
[lem-integral-ctf-equals-bc] (for $\mathcal O_E$ also [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]).
Preservation of $D^b_c$ by the operations, including general internal Hom
and the exceptional adjoint, is [sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability], with the
exceptional adjoint from [sk-thm-existence]; for integral internal
Hom see also [cor-coef-integral-internal-hom], [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction].
Verdier biduality is [sk-thm-pd-verdier-duality]: integrally by reduction
modulo $\pi_E$ and derived Nakayama ([thm-coef-integral-verdier]), for $E$
by integral models, for $\Qlb$ by descent to a finite $E$. The comparisons
with reduction and extension of scalars are [sk-prop-scalar-six]; they are
built from the same evaluation and adjunction maps.
